items.title: Fires break out at fuel station and flat construction site in Kochi
points: Two separate fire incidents were reported from the suburbs of Kochi city on Saturday, including at a fuel station.
In the first incident, the fire broke out at the fuel station at Moosarippady near Kolencherry around 6 am.
The blaze occurred as sparks caused by a short circuit at a pillar spread to the dispensing unit, according to officials with the Pattimattom fire station.
“The incident happened soon after the pump was opened and a major tragedy was averted as there were no customers at the facility,” the officials said.
In the other incident, a fire broke out at an apartment complex under construction at Cheranalloor around noon.
The blaze occurred on the first floor of the 19-storey building.
“The fire originated from the construction materials and spread to drain cell mats meant for gardening.
Firefighting units from the Eloor and Thrikkakara stations rushed to the spot and extinguished the blaze quickly,” an official with the Eloor station said.

items.title: Padmaja’s BJP exit reopens old wounds in Congress
points: Padmaja Venugopal’s exit from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has reopened old political fault lines in the Thrissur Congress, with her repeated allegations against local leaders and growing resistance to her possible return threatening to trigger fresh…
While the BJP has described her resignation as a personal decision, sections of the Congress in Thrissur have made it clear that her homecoming may not be a smooth affair.
Suresh termed the resignation of Ms. Venugopal, a National Council member and State Core Committee member, unfortunate.
He said she had been actively associated with the party over the past year as a special invitee to the State Core Committee and had received due recognition and responsibilities.
“Padmaja Venugopal occupied the position of an elder sister among party leaders and workers from Kasaragod to Thiruvananthapuram.
Union Minister of State and Thrissur MP Suresh Gopi, meanwhile, distanced himself from her induction into the BJP.
She contested the Assembly elections from Thrissur as Congress candidate in 2016 and 2021 but lost on both occasions.

items.title: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik gets MEA approval for Taj Mahal visit, but Nizamuddin Dargah request denied: Report
points: The government has reportedly approved Pakistan's climate change minister Musadik Malik's request to visit Taj Mahal in Agra.
However, his request to visit Nizamuddin Dargah in Delhi has been rejected.
The Pakistani delegation, led by Malik, will also visit other security-cleared locations in Delhi, including Humayun's Tomb and Dilli Haat, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.
The proposed visit to Nizamuddin Dargah has not been cleared by the security agencies and the ministry of external affairs.

Malik, who previously made harsh remarks against India over the Indus Waters Treaty, is in India for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, being hosted in New Delhi from November 20 to 22.
On Friday, Malik said that Pakistan will fully support all efforts to take forward peace and security in the region.
India has invited all 10 SCO member states, along with observer countries and dialogue partners, to participate in the inaugural forum.

items.title: 14-year-old hacker held for trying to sell private data of 4,000 Agniveers on dark web: Delhi Police
points: Investigation has revealed that artificial intelligence tools were allegedly used to access the information.

File | Photo Credit: Reuters A 14-year-old boy from Haryana's Ballabhgarh was apprehended by the Delhi Police Special Cell for allegedly hacking into a website and attempting to sell sensitive data linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web…

According to investigators, the juvenile gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in other government departments.
The Delhi Police's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile's digital devices.
The police have also written to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs seeking the official database of Agniveers to match it with the recovered information and verify its authenticity.

The incident has brought the security of digital platforms containing information related to Agniveer personnel under scrutiny, even as investigators work to establish the nature and scale of the alleged data breach.

items.title: Telangana Minister Mohd Azharuddin expresses disappointment over Siraj’s exclusion
points: In a post on a social media platform, Mr. Azharuddin expressed disappointment over Mr. Siraj’s exclusion, recalling his past performances.
“His performances, especially when Team India needed him in Bumrah’s absence, have shown his commitment, ability and fighting spirit.
He has consistently stepped up and delivered for the country,” he said.

While wishing young pacer Anshul Kamboj, who was included in the playing XI, the best, Mr. Azharuddin said Siraj deserved better consideration and hoped the team management explained the decision to him with the clarity and respect he deserved.
The Minister’s comments carry significance, as he is a leading political leader from Telangana.
Moreover, he understands the demands of international cricket as he led the country earlier, leaving an indelible mark as a player before he was sidelined over match-fixing allegations.

The controversy has also acquired a political and communal dimension, with a Congress MP alleging that religious considerations could have influenced the selection and questioning whether Mr. Siraj was being overlooked because he was a Muslim.

items.title: 'There are Shami, Sarfaraz too': Congress MP Masood says team selection should be merit-based
points: Selection to the Indian cricket team should be based on performance and not dictated by a player’s background, Congress MP Imran Masood said on Saturday, a day after he triggered a controversy by suggesting that pacer Mohammed Siraj was not picked for the…
Speaking to news agency ANI, the Saharanpur MP sought to downplay the row over his remarks on Siraj.
During the exchange, the reporter brought up questions raised in the past over Mohammed Shami’s exclusion from the playing XI.
Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket earlier this month.
“There’s Mohammed Shami, there’s Sarfaraz [Khan], and many others.
Selections should be based on performance; if someone is performing well, it shouldn’t matter where they come from...,” Masood said.
I find that completely unacceptable,” ANI quoted Congress Rajya Sabha MP Ranjeet Ranjan as saying.
Masood maintained that his remarks did not reflect the Congress’s views and that he had made them in his personal capacity.

Taking to Instagram, both leaders said they would be present at the meeting and the forum would be open to the youth of Goa to discuss their issues.

items.title: Two dead, one critical in Sagar after suspected spurious liquor consumption, samples sent for test: MP cops

The deceased were identified as Kamlesh Lodhi (45) and Chandrabhan Singh (42), both residents of Semra Ramchandra village in Shahgarh block.
According to family members, the two neighbours consumed liquor together on Thursday night.
They reportedly drank a locally available brand known as Lal Masala, following which their health deteriorated.
One of the men died at home, while the other died during treatment at Bundelkhand Medical College in Sagar.
Sagar additional superintendent of police Jaiveer Singh Bhadauria said both men had existing health complications.

Villagers have also alleged that Kamlesh used to sell liquor in the village.” Police and excise officials have launched an inquiry to trace the source of the liquor and ascertain whether it was spurious.

items.title: Gold Ring Helps Crack Rape-Murder Case, Suspect Arrested Within 6 Hours
points: A gold ring bearing hallmark details proved to be a crucial lead in identifying a 54-year-old woman who was sexually assaulted and murdered inside an unused railway coach at the Nagercoil railway yard in Tamil Nadu's Kanniyakumari district.
The crime occurred at midnight on November 13, inside a coach stationed at the railway yard.
With no immediate clues to establish her identity, railway police turned to the only identifiable possession she had on her - a gold ring featuring a serpent design.
According to Railway SP (Trichy) Adarsh Pachera, the hallmark details on the ring helped investigators trace its origins to Gujarat.
The seller there verified that the ring had been supplied to a retailer in Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
While identifying the victim itself was a major breakthrough, the police also cracked the rape and murder case swiftly, arresting the suspect within six hours of launching the investigation.
Tamil Nadu Railways DGP K Vannia Perumal complimented the investigation, particularly the efforts of the Railway SP.

items.title: Amid Freezing Cold, Ladakh Votes In Panchayat, Municipal Polls
points: Amid freezing cold, polling stared across Ladakh for Panchayat and municipal elections, marking the return of grassroots democracy in the region that was carved as a separate Union Territory in 2019.
Of the 192 Sarpanch seats, 55 candidates have already been elected unopposed, leaving 137 seats to be decided through polling today.
Similarly, 1,186 candidates for Panch positions have been elected unopposed out of 1,428 seats, with voting taking place for 242 Panchs only.
In the municipal polls, voting is taking place across all 21 wards of Leh Municipal Council.
In Kargil four out of the 17 wards in Kargil Municipal Council have been elected unopposed.
The first major democratic exercise is taking place amid political unrest and protests by Ladakhi groups represented by the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance.
As per an official notification, the Panchayat election process will conclude by November 30.
On December 4, Ladakh will vote for crucial Hill Councils elections across all 8 districts.

points: A Delhi fast-track court on Saturday formally framed charges against all 14 accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.

The accused pleaded not guilty before Special Judge Ajay Gupta at the Rouse Avenue Courts and opted to face trial in the alleged conspiracy that led to the cancellation of the medical entrance examination in May.
The NEET-UG examination was held on May 3, 2026, with around 22 lakh candidates appearing for it.
The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the examination on May 12 after allegations of a question paper leak emerged and subsequently conducted a re-examination on June 21.

On November 18, Special Judge Ajay Gupta directed that charges be framed against the accused for criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, destruction of evidence, and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public…
The court scheduled November 21 for the formal framing of charges, directing all the accused to appear in person from judicial custody.

items.title: India Beats USA In Electric Car Penetration
points: Electric cars accounted for a larger proportion of new passenger-car registrations in India than in the United States in September 2026.
According to figures highlighted by former NITI Aayog CEO Amitabh Kant, battery-electric cars made up 8.8% of new registrations here, against 6.8% in the US.
India has not overtaken America in the total number of electric cars sold.
In 2025, India's battery-electric share of new car registrations was 4.3%, compared with 7.5% in the US.
In September 2026, the respective monthly figures stood at 8.8% and 6.8%.
The 2019–2025 figures are annual shares, while September 2026 is a single month.
If 100 new cars are registered and nine are battery EVs, the penetration rate is around 9%.

According to government figures cited in the report, 67,657 EV chargers had been installed across states and Union Territories as of 7 August 2026, including chargers associated with battery-swapping locations.

items.title: Taiwan Widens Short Sale Curbs After Shares Plunge on AI Concern
points: (Bloomberg) -- Taiwan widened curbs on short sales of local stocks and said it has been buying shares, stepping up efforts to revive confidence after the island’s benchmark index had its worst weekly fall in 35 years.

The Financial Supervisory Commission imposed a blanket ban on short selling below the previous trading day’s closing price, covering both margin short sales and borrowed shares, it said in a statement Saturday.
Separately, the island’s NT$500 billion ($15 billion) National Financial Stabilization Fund said it has entered the market to support Taiwanese stocks and urged investors to remain confident.
23, marks the third time this month that authorities have unveiled short-selling curbs to tame market volatility.
Taiwan’s tech-heavy stock market has witnessed heavy selloffs as the global artificial intelligence trade came under strain, sending the island’s benchmark to its worst week since 1991.

points: Velankanni Raj Less than a month after sanctioning 2,880 infrastructure works worth ₹376.65 crore across urban local bodies, the Tamil Nadu government has approved another 1,604 projects worth ₹386.91 crore for 2026-27.
The projects were approved at the second meeting of the Common Project Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee held on October 27, 2026.

The Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department issued two Government Orders on November 18, according administrative sanction to these works under the Chief Minister’s Integrated Urban Development Mission (CMIUDM).
Of the total, 730 projects worth ₹132.333 crore will be taken up in municipalities and corporations, excluding Greater Chennai Corporation.
Of the total projects approved, the majority relates to roads — 1,540 road works have been approved across Tamil Nadu.
Over 253 km of roads in municipalities, corporations, and town panchayats and are set to be laid or renewed under the fresh ₹386.91-crore infrastructure package.

The government has identified 23,500 acres of government land across 31 districts, sufficient for about 4.70 lakh sites.
The proposed Niveshana Yojane will provide sites to eligible landless families, including ex-servicemen, with a 3% reservation for former defence personnel.

items.title: Pak Minister In Delhi Calls For Talks Via Culture, Joint Mechanism On Terror
points: More cultural engagement between India and Pakistan can open new avenues for dialogue between the two neighbours whose relations have remained strained since the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik…

Culture had a key role in bringing countries together even when political differences prevented direct engagement, Malik said on the sidelines of the first Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi.
His comments come during the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister to India since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari attended a SCO meeting in Goa in May 2023.

The visit assumes significance in view of the existing diplomatic tensions between New Delhi and Islamabad, particularly after India put the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance after the Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people.
Asked whether relations between India and Pakistan could improve after the forum, Malik said he was hopeful that the regional relationships would move forward.

points: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday reiterated that Kashmir doesn't have any local terrorists left.

His remarks came days after security forces killed LeT commander Mohammed Lateef Bhat in Kulgam.
Shah made similar remarks a few days back, calling the absence of any India-born terrorist in J&K for the first time in 35 years a “significant milestone”.

"With the elimination of Lashkar (Lashkar-e-Taiba) terrorist Lateef Bhat, the entire Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists," he had said, addressing the annual anti-terror conference in Delhi on Thursday.

points: Photo: X/@CMofKarnataka via ANI The Karnataka Government will make a fresh attempt to secure Scheduled Tribe (ST) status for the Kadugolla (Adavigolla) and Hattigolla communities after five rejections of its earlier proposals by the Centre.
The State Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister D.K.
Shivakumar on November 19, decided to renew its recommendation to the Union Government after obtaining fresh evidence through a comprehensive ethnographic study.
Karnataka has been pursuing the demand for inclusion of the Kadugolla community in the ST list since 2015.
The State sent proposals and additional communications to the Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs between March 2015 and April 2025.

items.title: Automakers to Govt: Give Plug-In Hybrid Range Extender Cars The Same Benefits As EVs
points: Car manufacturers are preparing to ask the government to treat plug-in hybrid vehicles more favourably under the upcoming Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE)-III rules.
Their request is simple: give plug-in hybrids the same regulatory credit as fully electric cars and range-extended EVs when calculating how efficiently a manufacturer's entire range performs.
It concerns the accounting system used to determine whether carmakers meet stricter fleet fuel-consumption targets, which take effect from 1 April 2027.
Under the rules notified on 30 September 2026, a battery-electric car receives a 'super-credit' multiplier of 3.0.
A range-extended electric vehicle also receives 3.0, while a plug-in hybrid gets 2.5.
A conventional strong hybrid receives a smaller multiplier of 1.6.
The CAFE-III framework becomes progressively tougher between April 2027 and March 2032.
Its reference fuel-consumption benchmark moves from 3.996 litres per 100 km in 2027-28 to 3.3273 litres per 100 km by 2031-32.

points: The commission said the move was aimed at ensuring measurable pollution reduction at the ground level and fixing accountability, as it called on the governments of Delhi and NCR states to prepare comprehensive action plans for the coming year.

items.title: 'Rename Nagpur as Deekshabhoomi': Sanjay Raut's demand amid Dadar Metro renaming row
points: Sanjay Raut is advocating for the renaming of Nagpur to Deekshabhoomi as a tribute to Dr B R Ambedkar.
The demand comes after Maharashtra government's plan to change Dadar Metro station to Chaityabhoomi.
